Filter maintenance and water changes are crucial for long term water clarity, but sometimes the debris in the water causing it to be cloudy can be so small that it slips through the filter quite easily. This is where water clarifying agents like these AquaPacs can help. They bind up these smaller particles into larger conglomerates that are more easily pulled from the water by the filter. Cleaning a fish tank doesn’t always mean draining it. In this method, waste and debris are removed while the water stays in place. Tools like siphon vacuums and filtration systems pull out uneaten food, algae, and sediment from the gravel, keeping the environment clean without stressing the fish. What makes this approach effective is balance. Beneficial bacteria remain undisturbed, water chemistry stays stable, and the tank continues to cycle naturally. It’s a low-impact way to maintain a healthy aquarium, showing how smart maintenance can work with the ecosystem instead of resetting it.

Sunday is tank clean day! ☀️ Cleaning your aquarium is an important part of maintaining a healthy environment for your fishy pals🐠🐟 I clean my tanks once a week because i have a lot of fish who live to eat which means they poop a lot.  An important part of my cleaning schedule includes scrubbing the insides of the glass to remove any algae that has built up. I also remove and rinse my internal filter once a week to remove the build up of gunk so that it doesn’t get clogged up and stop working.  #aquarium #fishtank #aquariumfish #cichlids #cleantok

Water Change Technique (as per request) #fish #plants #aquarium #aquascape FISHROOM OVERVIEW Water/Aquarium Parameters pH = 7.8 Hardness = 250 mg CaC02 Exact water chemistry can be found at the following link: https://www.reddeer.ca/city-services/water-wastewater--stormwater/water/water-quality/ Temperature = The majority are heated by in-floor heating: 68 - 72F (20-22C). Several tanks (7) are heated to about 78F or 25C Nitrate = 20-30 ppm (average) Light Low - Low-end Marina, Aquarium Masters and Aqueon LED fixtures (15 hrs/day) Moderate - Nicrew, Hygger 24/7 and 957 and Current Satellite (15 hrs/day) High - Fluval Planted 2.0 (90 gallon aquarium - 12 hrs/day) Water change = 25 - 50% weekly (most at 25-30%). Seachem Prime as a conditioner. Filtration = Aquaclear HangOnBacks, Ehiem canisters and various internal canister/sponge filters (Marina, fluval, AquaEL) Substrate = sand and gravel, but mostly sand. Estes Stony River sand is the substrate of choice – resists compaction Fertilization - Fish waste (go, poop!) - Root tabs = osmocote capsules (from Rich Cowboy!) and API root tabs. In general, I only use for heavy root feeders, fairly regularly for Amazon swords, Tiger lotus and Madagascar lace and just the odd one for other plants that benefit from them, basically just when I see their growth lagging. - No added CO2 or liquid fertilizers Clean up crew -Ramshorn, bladder and Malaysian trumpet snails -Neocaridina shrimp Plants Easy - Anubias barteri - Bacopa monnieri - Bucephalandra sp. "kedagang, " wavy green," and "purple blue?" - Ceratophyllum demersum (hornwort) -fast grower - Cryptocoryne crispatula "balansae," lutea, nevelli, pontederiifolia, spiralis, usteriana, wendtii - Eleocharis montevidensis (giant hairgrass) - Hydrophila polysperma (fast grower) and corymbosa "compact" - Hydrocotyle tripartita, vulgaris - Lemna minor (Duckweed)- fast grower - Limnophila sessiliflora -fast grower - Lomariopsis lineata (Susswassertang) - Pistia stratiotes (Water lettuce) -fast grower - Schismatoglottis prietoi (the Schnizz!) - Vallisneria nana and spiralis - Vesicularia dubyana (Java moss) - Vesicularia sp.
